topics.title: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling & Bottlenecks
topics.summary: Hardware limits vs commodity clustering, stateless web tiers, and DB read/write scaling.
topics.key_intuition: Vertical has hardware ceilings and SPOF. Horizontal requires stateless web services, LBs, and partitioned databases.
topics.pitfalls: Treating DBs as horizontally scalable without planning for replication lag and distributed transactions.
topics.notes:
### Horizontal Scaling Architecture
- Stateless web services behind LBs
- DB read replicas for read-heavy workloads
- Partitioning / Sharding for write scaling
- Distributed Redis sessions

topics.title: Load Balancers & Algorithms (L4 vs L7, NGINX, HAProxy, Envoy)
topics.summary: Transport (L4 TCP/UDP) vs Application (L7 HTTP/Headers) routing algorithms and health checking.
topics.key_intuition: L4 routes on IP & Port (fast, low CPU). L7 inspects HTTP headers, path, cookies (smart routing, TLS termination, microservice path routing).
topics.pitfalls: Sticky sessions causing uneven traffic hotspotting; unmonitored unhealthy nodes receiving traffic.
topics.notes:
### Key Algorithms
- Round Robin, Weighted Round Robin
- Least Connections
- Consistent Hashing
- Active vs Passive Health Checks

topics.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
topics.summary: Partitioning data across distributed nodes such that node scaling only reshuffles k/N keys.
topics.key_intuition: Hash ring [0, 2^32 - 1]. Virtual nodes (100-200 per physical host) eliminate non-uniform distribution and hotspots.
topics.pitfalls: Standard hash % N remaps 100% of keys on scale event, causing cache stampedes.
topics.notes:
### Consistent Hashing Ring
- Add node: only steals keys from clockwise neighbor.
- Virtual nodes smooth distribution variance across servers.

topics.title: Caching Strategies & Eviction (Cache-Aside, Write-Back, Stampede)
topics.summary: Cache-Aside, Write-Through, Write-Behind, Refresh-Ahead patterns with LRU/LFU eviction and stampede mitigation.
topics.key_intuition: Cache-Aside is resilient to cache crashes. Write-Behind batches DB writes for lowest write latency, but risks data loss on cache crash. Thundering herd prevented with mutex locks.
topics.pitfalls: Cache Stampede / Thundering Herd when hot key expires; omitting TTL causing memory leaks.
topics.notes:
### Caching Patterns Table
1. Cache-Aside (Standard)
2. Write-Through
3. Write-Behind (Batched)
4. Eviction: LRU, LFU, TTL

topics.title: CAP Theorem & PACELC Trade-offs (Consistency Models)
topics.summary: Constraints between Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance in distributed networks.
topics.key_intuition: Partitions (P) are inevitable in distributed WANs. Under partition: choose Consistency (CP) or Availability (AP). PACELC: Else Latency or Consistency.
topics.pitfalls: Claiming a distributed WAN system is CA (CA only exists in single-node/single-datacenter contexts).
topics.notes:
### PACELC Framework
- If Partition (P): Availability (A) vs Consistency (C)
- Else (E): Latency (L) vs Consistency (C)

topics.title: Database Sharding & Partitioning Strategies (Range, Hash, Directory)
topics.summary: Horizontal partitioning of database records across multiple database instances, resharding, and routing.
topics.key_intuition: Choose Shard Key carefully! Must distribute read/write traffic evenly without cross-shard joins. Strategies: Hash, Range, Directory.
topics.pitfalls: Celebrity/Hotspot problem where one key gets 90% of traffic; cross-shard distributed transactions.
topics.notes:
### Sharding Trade-offs
- High write scalability
- Cross-shard queries require scatter-gather (slow)
- Resharding requires zero-downtime dual-writes

topics.title: Relational (ACID) vs NoSQL (Document, Key-Value, Wide-Column, Graph)
topics.summary: Structural tradeoffs: relational normalization and ACID guarantees vs document flexibility, key-value speed, and wide-column analytics.
topics.key_intuition: RDBMS for strict transactional integrity and relational queries. Key-Value (Redis) for microsecond lookups. Document (MongoDB) for nested JSON. Wide-Column (Cassandra) for write-heavy time-series.
topics.pitfalls: Choosing NoSQL just for hype, then manually implementing joins and two-phase commits in application code.
topics.notes:
### Database Selection Guide
- Relational: Financial, inventory, strict ACID
- Document: User profiles, content catalogs
- Wide-Column: IoT telemetry, chat histories, analytics
- Graph: Social networks, fraud detection

topics.title: Message Queues & Event Streaming (Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs SQS)
topics.summary: Message brokers vs distributed commit logs: push vs pull models, ordering guarantees, consumer groups, and backpressure.
topics.key_intuition: RabbitMQ is a smart broker/dumb consumer (routing keys, transient queues, push). Kafka is a dumb broker/smart consumer (append-only disk log, partition ordering, replayability, pull).
topics.pitfalls: Using Kafka as a transient task queue with thousands of short-lived topics, or RabbitMQ as a permanent historical audit log.
topics.notes:
### Broker vs Log
- RabbitMQ: Complex routing, transient task workers, per-message ACK.
- Kafka: High throughput (millions/sec), partitioned log, offset tracking, replayable.

topics.title: Distributed Transactions & The Saga Pattern (Orchestration vs Choreography)
topics.summary: Overcoming lack of 2-Phase Commit (2PC) across microservices using Sagas, compensating transactions, and the Outbox Pattern.
topics.key_intuition: 2PC is blocking and fragile. Saga executes sequential local transactions with compensating rollbacks on failure. Choreography (events) for simple flows; Orchestration for complex workflows.
topics.pitfalls: Dual-write bug: writing to database and publishing to message broker without the Transactional Outbox pattern.
topics.notes:
### Transactional Outbox Pattern
1. Write business entity AND outbox message in same local DB transaction.
2. Debezium / Background worker polls outbox and publishes to broker.
3. Guarantees at-least-once message delivery!

topics.title: Database Replication, Quorum & Replication Lag (Sync vs Async)
topics.summary: Single-leader, multi-leader, and leaderless replication, read-after-write consistency, and quorum math.
topics.key_intuition: Synchronous replication guarantees zero data loss (RPO=0) but spikes latency. Asynchronous is fast but risks data loss on failover. Quorum R + W > N guarantees reading the latest write.
topics.pitfalls: Split-brain in leader elections during network partitions; users reading stale data immediately after updating their profile (fix with read-after-write routing).
topics.notes:
### Quorum Equation
- N = Replicas (e.g. 3)
- W = Write quorum (e.g. 2)
- R = Read quorum (e.g. 2)
- R + W > N ensures at least one node has latest version timestamp.

topics.title: API Protocols & Data Serialization (REST, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSockets)
topics.summary: Comparing communication protocols: text JSON vs binary Protobuf, client-driven schemas vs server contracts, and streaming.
topics.key_intuition: REST for public developer APIs. gRPC (HTTP/2 + Protobuf) for low-latency internal microservices. GraphQL for mobile aggregators avoiding over-fetching. WebSockets for bidirectional real-time feeds.
topics.pitfalls: Using GraphQL internally between microservices creating N+1 query waterfalls; using WebSockets when unidirectional SSE suffices.
topics.notes:
### Protocol Trade-offs
- REST: Human-readable, ubiquitous, stateless.
- gRPC: 7-10x smaller payload, multiplexed HTTP/2, contract-first.
- WebSockets: Persistent full-duplex TCP connection.

topics.title: Distributed Unique ID Generation (Snowflake, ULID, UUIDv7)
topics.summary: Generating 64-bit and 128-bit globally unique, time-sortable IDs at scale without central database bottlenecks.
topics.key_intuition: Twitter Snowflake generates 64-bit IDs (41b timestamp, 10b worker ID, 12b sequence) sortable by time. UUIDv4 destroys B-tree index locality; UUIDv7 / ULID use timestamp prefixes to maintain B-tree performance.
topics.pitfalls: Clock drift / NTP backwards adjustments causing duplicate IDs in Snowflake; using random UUIDv4 as primary keys on high-volume MySQL/Postgres tables.
topics.notes:
### Snowflake Bit Layout (64-bit)
- 1 bit: Unused (sign bit)
- 41 bits: Epoch milliseconds (~69 years)
- 10 bits: Machine / Node ID (1024 nodes)
- 12 bits: Sequence counter (4096 IDs per ms per node)

topics.title: Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bitly)
topics.summary: High availability read-heavy short URL generation and redirect service handling billions of links.
topics.key_intuition: Base62 encoding of 64-bit unique ID (Snowflake). 7 chars = 62^7 ≈ 3.5T URLs. 301 vs 302 redirect (302 enables analytics tracking). Redis cache for hot redirects.
topics.pitfalls: MD5/SHA256 hash collision truncation; using 301 permanent redirect when click tracking is required.
topics.notes:
### TinyURL Architecture
- Reads: Redis cache, 302 redirect.
- Writes: Unique ID Generator -> Base62 -> DB record.
- Scalability: 100:1 Read-to-Write ratio.

topics.title: Design a Distributed Rate Limiter
topics.summary: Scalable multi-tier rate limiting service protecting internal microservices from DDoS and abuse.
topics.key_intuition: API Gateway middleware + Redis sliding window counter with atomic Lua script. HTTP 429 Too Many Requests + Retry-After header.
topics.pitfalls: Single Redis instance failure blocking all traffic (fail-open vs fail-close trade-off); race conditions without Lua atomicity.
topics.notes:
### Rate Limiter Blueprint
- Token bucket in-memory buffer with periodic sync to Redis.
- Partitioned by API Key or IP address.
- Fallback to local token bucket if Redis is unreachable.

topics.title: Design a Real-Time Chat System (WhatsApp / Slack)
topics.summary: Real-time messaging architecture with 1-on-1 and group chats, presence detection, and durable message persistence.
topics.key_intuition: Persistent WebSockets on Chat Gateway servers. Redis PubSub for presence & ephemeral routing. Cassandra partitioned by chat_id for fast sequential timeline queries.
topics.pitfalls: Storing chat messages in relational DB with unbounded foreign keys; group fanout overhead for massive channels.
topics.notes:
### Chat Architecture
- WebSocket connection servers
- Cassandra: Partition key = chat_id, Clustering key = message_id.
- Presence service with 30s heartbeat.

topics.title: Design a Video Streaming Platform (YouTube / Netflix)
topics.summary: Video ingestion, transcoding DAG, adaptive bitrate packaging, and global CDN delivery pipeline for millions of concurrent viewers.
topics.key_intuition: Adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH) chunks (1080p, 720p, 480p). Storage on S3 + edge CDNs. Distributed transcoding workers consuming queue tasks.
topics.pitfalls: Serving raw video files directly from origin servers; synchronous video encoding on web API servers.
topics.notes:
### Video Ingestion Pipeline
- Client uploads chunked video to Object Storage.
- S3 trigger -> Message Queue -> Transcoding Workers (FFmpeg) -> Multi-resolution chunks + .m3u8 playlist.
- CDN caches video segments near users.

topics.title: Design an E-Commerce Flash Sale & Inventory Reservation System
topics.summary: Ultra-high concurrency checkout system handling 100,000 req/sec for limited stock items with zero overselling.
topics.key_intuition: Never hit relational DB for inventory checks during flash sales! Pre-warm Redis with stock counters; use atomic DECR via Lua scripts. Temporary reservation with TTL (10 min checkout window). Async Kafka order queue.
topics.pitfalls: Database row-level lock contention on product record crashing DB; overselling inventory due to race conditions.
topics.notes:
### Flash Sale Architecture
1. API Gateway with Token Bucket rate limiter
2. Redis stock decrement: atomic DECR via Lua script
3. Push order intent to Kafka -> Order workers write DB asynchronously

topics.title: Design a Distributed Web Crawler & Search Indexer (Google Bot)
topics.summary: Scalable web crawler discovering, fetching, deduplicating, and indexing billions of web pages.
topics.key_intuition: URL Frontier with politeness queues (delay between requests to same domain) and priority queues. DNS caching to avoid DNS bottleneck. SimHash for near-duplicate HTML page detection.
topics.pitfalls: Spider traps (infinite loops on dynamic URLs); violating robots.txt; hitting target web servers too aggressively.
topics.notes:
### URL Frontier Design
- Priority Queues (PageRank importance)
- Queue Router -> Politeness Queues (one queue per hostname)
- Worker threads pull from politeness queues with rate limiters

topics.title: Design a Distributed Key-Value Store (DynamoDB / Cassandra)
topics.summary: Highly available, partitioned distributed key-value storage system with tunable consistency and LSM-Trees.
topics.key_intuition: Consistent hashing ring with virtual nodes. Gossip protocol for failure detection. Sloppy quorum and hinted handoff for high write availability. LSM-Trees (MemTable + WAL + SSTables) on disk.
topics.pitfalls: Read amplification when SSTable compaction lags behind; vector clock conflicts during concurrent writes.
topics.notes:
### LSM-Tree Write Path
1. Write to Write-Ahead Log (WAL) on disk for durability.
2. Write to in-memory MemTable (SkipList).
3. When MemTable is full, flush to disk as immutable SSTable.
4. Background compaction merges SSTables.

topics.title: Design a Proximity Service / Nearby Places (Yelp / Google Maps)
topics.summary: Geospatial search query system returning top businesses or drivers within a specific radius of a user.
topics.key_intuition: Geohashing (Base32 representation of interleaved lat/lon bits) or Google S2 / Uber H3 hexagonal cells. Query matches prefix of current cell and 8 adjacent neighbors. In-memory indexing with Redis GEO.
topics.pitfalls: Using naive SQL `WHERE sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) < R` full table scan across millions of coordinates.
topics.notes:
### Geohash Precision
- Length 5: ~4.9 km x 4.9 km
- Length 6: ~1.2 km x 0.6 km (Ideal for city search)
- Query: Search current Geohash prefix + 8 adjacent cells to solve boundary edge cases.

topics.title: Design a Ride-Sharing Dispatch System (Uber / Lyft)
topics.summary: Real-time driver location tracking, geospatial indexing, ride matching, and dynamic surge pricing.
topics.key_intuition: Drivers send GPS ping every 4s via WebSocket. Location ingestion service updates in-memory geospatial index (Uber H3 cells in Redis). Match engine queries nearby available drivers, computes ETA, and offers trip.
topics.pitfalls: Persisting every raw GPS ping to disk DB; driver acceptance race conditions where two drivers accept same ride.
topics.notes:
### Ride Dispatch Pipeline
- Driver Location Service: Ingests 4s pings into Redis Geospatial / H3 index.
- Trip Management Service: Rider requests trip -> Match Engine queries H3 cell -> Dispatches offer via push notification with 15s TTL.

topics.title: Design a Social Network News Feed (Twitter / Instagram)
topics.summary: Feed generation and ranking architecture for hundreds of millions of users with diverse follower distributions.
topics.key_intuition: Hybrid fanout architecture: Fanout-on-write (push) for standard users (insert post ID into followers Redis feed lists). Fanout-on-read (pull) for celebrity accounts with millions of followers.
topics.pitfalls: Fanout-on-write for celebrities like Elon Musk (writing 100M redis entries takes minutes and overwhelms queues).
topics.notes:
### Hybrid Fanout Strategy
- Users with < 20,000 followers: Fanout-on-write (push to follower feed caches).
- Celebrity users (> 20,000 followers): Fanout-on-read (merge dynamically at read time).

topics.title: Design a Distributed Notification Service (APNs / FCM)
topics.summary: Scalable multi-channel notification platform handling millions of push notifications, SMS, and emails per second.
topics.key_intuition: Rate limiting per user and vendor. Prioritization queues (High: OTP/2FA, Medium: Transactions, Low: Marketing). Integration with APNs, FCM, Twilio with retry and circuit breakers.
topics.pitfalls: Marketing notifications delaying critical time-sensitive OTP security messages; retry storms crashing downstream vendors.
topics.notes:
### Priority Queues & Workers
- High Priority: OTP / Authentication (zero queue delay)
- Medium Priority: Order confirmations, chat alerts
- Low Priority: Promotional newsletters
- Circuit Breaker on 3rd-party vendor outages

topics.title: Design a Distributed Task Scheduler & Job Orchestrator
topics.summary: Scalable distributed cron and delayed execution system capable of scheduling and executing millions of jobs at exact times.
topics.key_intuition: Time-partitioned delayed task queues using Redis Sorted Sets (`ZADD timestamp jobId`) or Kafka with partition timestamp indexing. Distributed worker heartbeat and lease lock mechanism to prevent duplicate execution.
topics.pitfalls: Split-brain leading to double execution of sensitive tasks (financial payments); timer drift across distributed worker nodes.
topics.notes:
### Delayed Queue Mechanics
- Producer: ZADD delayed_tasks <scheduled_timestamp> <taskId>
- Poller Worker: ZRANGEBYSCORE delayed_tasks 0 <now_timestamp> LIMIT 100
- Atomic pop using Lua script, then push to active execution queue.

topics.title: Design a Metrics Monitoring & Alerting System (Prometheus / Datadog)
topics.summary: High-throughput telemetry ingestion, time-series storage, downsampling, and automated alerting engine.
topics.key_intuition: Pull model (Prometheus scraper) vs Push model (statsd daemon). Time-Series Database (TSDB) with delta-of-delta timestamp compression (Gorilla). Multi-tiered retention and downsampling rollups.
topics.pitfalls: High-cardinality label explosion (e.g. user_id as metric label) causing memory explosion in TSDB index; alert flapping.
topics.notes:
### TSDB Downsampling Tiers
- Raw metrics: Retained 7 days (10s resolution)
- 1-minute Rollup: Retained 30 days (avg, min, max, p99)
- 1-hour Rollup: Retained 1 year
- Alert rules evaluated against sliding windows

topics.title: Classes vs Records vs Structs
topics.summary: Value types vs Reference types, value equality in records, with-expressions, and stack vs heap allocations.
topics.key_intuition: Structs on stack (avoid boxing!). Records are classes with compiler synthesized value-based equality and "with" mutation: ideal for DTOs and immutable events.
topics.pitfalls: Boxing structs when casting to object or interfaces; mutating mutable structs; large structs (> 16 bytes) incurring copy cost.
topics.notes:
### C# Type Comparison
- Class: Reference type on Heap
- Record Class: Synthesized value equality, immutable by default, with keyword
- Record Struct: Value type on Stack, zero heap allocations
- readonly struct: Compiler enforces immutability; avoids defensive copying.

topics.title: Interfaces, Generics & Generic Constraints
topics.summary: Decoupling implementations with interfaces, type parameter constraints, and generic repositories.
topics.key_intuition: Generics eliminate runtime casting and boxing. Generic constraints (where T : class, IEntity, new()) enforce compile-time safety.
topics.pitfalls: Creating generic repository anti-patterns that leak IQueryable and hide EF Core capabilities.
topics.notes:
### Generic Constraints Cheat Sheet
- where T : struct
- where T : class
- where T : notnull
- where T : new()
- where T : BaseClass, IInterface

topics.title: LINQ & Deferred Execution (IEnumerable vs IQueryable)
topics.summary: Deferred execution hazards (multiple enumeration), and IEnumerable in-memory vs IQueryable SQL expression trees.
topics.key_intuition: LINQ queries execute only when enumerated. IQueryable translates expression trees to SQL; IEnumerable runs in C# memory. Calling .ToList() too early pulls entire tables into RAM!
topics.pitfalls: Multiple enumeration: iterating an unmaterialized IEnumerable twice executes the underlying query or API call twice! Use .ToList() before re-enumerating.
topics.notes:
### IEnumerable vs IQueryable
- IQueryable<T>: Uses Expression<Func<T, bool>>, translated to SQL by EF Core.
- IEnumerable<T>: Uses compiled Func<T, bool>, evaluated in .NET memory.
topics.code_snippet:
// SQL query with WHERE Status = 1
IQueryable<Order> query = dbContext.Orders.Where(o => o.Status == OrderStatus.Completed);

topics.title: Delegates, Func/Action & Events
topics.summary: Type-safe function pointers, Func<T, TResult>, Action<T>, and event-driven decoupling.
topics.key_intuition: Action represents void methods; Func represents methods returning a value. Predicate<T> returns bool. Events encapsulate delegates with add/remove accessors.
topics.pitfalls: Memory leaks when subscribing to events without unsubscribing (publisher holds strong reference to subscriber).
topics.notes:
### Delegate Best Practices
- Prefer built-in Action and Func over custom delegate definitions.
- Use WeakReference or IDisposable to unsubscribe events.
topics.code_snippet:
public event EventHandler<OrderCreatedEventArgs>? OrderCreated;
protected virtual void OnOrderCreated(OrderCreatedEventArgs e) => OrderCreated?.Invoke(this, e);

topics.title: IDisposable, Finalizers & IAsyncDisposable
topics.summary: Deterministic unmanaged resource cleanup, using var statements, and await using for asynchronous streams.
topics.key_intuition: GC only manages CLR memory. Unmanaged resources (file handles, DB connections, sockets) require deterministic cleanup via IDisposable.Dispose(). await using prevents thread blocking during I/O teardown.
topics.pitfalls: Leaking DB connections or HttpClient instances; suppressing finalizers without calling GC.SuppressFinalize(this).
topics.notes:
### Dispose Pattern Best Practices
- Use using var x = new Resource();
- For I/O teardown, implement IAsyncDisposable with await using.
- Always call GC.SuppressFinalize(this) in Dispose().

topics.title: async / await State Machine & Task Internals
topics.summary: How C# transforms async methods into state machine structs, Task completion, and non-blocking continuation callbacks.
topics.key_intuition: await does NOT block OS threads. When I/O begins, the thread returns to ThreadPool. When I/O completes via OS completion ports, ThreadPool resumes execution.
topics.pitfalls: Sync-over-async (.Result or .Wait()) starves ThreadPool threads and causes deadlocks! Never block on Tasks in ASP.NET Core.
topics.notes:
### Key Rules for Async in .NET
1. Async all the way down.
2. Never call .Result or .Wait().
3. Use ValueTask<T> when operations frequently complete synchronously (e.g. cache hit).

topics.title: Task.WhenAll, Concurrency & CancellationToken
topics.summary: Running multiple asynchronous tasks concurrently, cooperative cancellation propagation, and aggregating multi-task exceptions.
topics.key_intuition: Task.WhenAll launches independent I/O tasks concurrently: 3 calls taking 100ms finish in ~100ms total. CancellationToken enables graceful cancellation when clients disconnect.
topics.pitfalls: Forgetting to pass CancellationToken to DB/HTTP calls; ignoring OperationCanceledException.
topics.notes:
### Task.WhenAll with CancellationToken
- Pass ct to all child calls.
- Task.WhenAll aggregates all inner exceptions in task.Exception.InnerExceptions.

topics.title: ConfigureAwait(false) & SynchronizationContext
topics.summary: When ConfigureAwait matters: ASP.NET Core has no SynchronizationContext, but class libraries targeting general .NET must use ConfigureAwait(false).
topics.key_intuition: ASP.NET Core has NO SynchronizationContext: all continuations resume on arbitrary ThreadPool threads. ConfigureAwait(false) is redundant in controllers, but mandatory in shared NuGet libraries.
topics.pitfalls: Thinking ASP.NET Core controllers need ConfigureAwait(false); omitting it in reusable library code consumed by desktop/WPF apps.
topics.notes:
### ConfigureAwait Summary
- ASP.NET Core Controllers & Services: Not required.
- Reusable NuGet Class Libraries: Always use .ConfigureAwait(false).

topics.title: Middleware Pipeline Execution & Custom Middleware
topics.summary: HTTP requests and responses travelling through delegates in ASP.NET Core: execution order and short-circuiting.
topics.key_intuition: Russian doll execution order: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> Endpoint -> 3 -> 2 -> 1. Short-circuiting happens when a middleware returns early without calling next().
topics.pitfalls: Ordering bugs! Putting UseAuthorization() before UseAuthentication(); placing error handling middleware after components that throw.
topics.notes:
### Canonical Middleware Order
1. ExceptionHandler
2. Hsts
3. Routing
4. Cors
5. Authentication
6. Authorization
7. Custom business middleware
8. Endpoints

topics.title: Controllers vs Minimal APIs & Route Handling
topics.summary: Trade-offs between Controller-based APIs and high-performance Minimal APIs, endpoint routing, and TypedResults.
topics.key_intuition: Minimal APIs bypass heavy MVC reflection and action filter pipelines, yielding faster startup times and higher req/sec. TypedResults in .NET 7/8 provides strong typing for OpenAPI.
topics.pitfalls: Dumping hundreds of minimal API endpoints into Program.cs without modular extension methods.
topics.notes:
### Minimal APIs Best Practices
- Organize using route group extension methods.
- Return Results.Ok() or TypedResults.Ok<T>().

topics.title: Validation (FluentValidation) & Action/Exception Filters
topics.summary: Separating request validation rules from models using FluentValidation, and managing cross-cutting concerns with filters.
topics.key_intuition: FluentValidation separates validation logic into testable validator classes. Return RFC 7807 ValidationProblemDetails on failure.
topics.pitfalls: Putting business logic inside validation rules (e.g. database lookups in simple validators); throwing exceptions for standard validation errors.
topics.notes:
### FluentValidation Setup
- AbstractValidator<CreateOrderRequest>
- RuleFor(x => x.Email).NotEmpty().EmailAddress();
- Return standard RFC 7807 ValidationProblemDetails.

topics.title: Service Lifetimes & The Captive Dependency Trap
topics.summary: Transient vs Scoped vs Singleton, service provider scopes, and detecting the dreaded Captive Dependency bug.
topics.key_intuition: Singleton = created once. Scoped = once per HTTP request. Transient = new instance every injection. CAPTIVE DEPENDENCY BUG: Injecting Scoped into Singleton captures it forever, causing memory leaks and DbContext concurrency crashes!
topics.pitfalls: Injecting DbContext (Scoped) into a BackgroundService (Singleton); not enabling DI scope validation in Development.

topics.title: SQL: Joins, Indexes (Clustered vs Non-Clustered) & Execution Plans
topics.summary: Relational query mechanics, Index Seek vs Index Scan, Clustered (B-Tree data leaf) vs Non-Clustered indexes, and query profiling.
topics.key_intuition: Clustered index defines physical order of table on disk (1 per table). Non-clustered index is a separate B-tree mapping to clustered key. Index Seek traverses in O(log N); Index Scan reads whole index. Covering indexes include queried columns, avoiding Key Lookups.
topics.pitfalls: Applying functions to indexed columns in WHERE clause (WHERE YEAR(CreatedDate) = 2026) breaks index sargability, forcing full table scans!
topics.notes:
### SQL Optimization Checklist
1. Sargable WHERE clauses (no functions on columns).
2. Index Seek vs Scan in execution plan.
3. Include columns to avoid Key Lookups.
4. Avoid NOLOCK without understanding dirty read implications.

topics.title: EF Core: AsNoTracking, Change Tracker & Read Performance
topics.summary: Optimizing Entity Framework Core read queries by disabling identity resolution and change tracking snapshots with .AsNoTracking().
topics.key_intuition: By default, EF Core takes a memory snapshot of loaded entities to detect mutations for SaveChangesAsync(). For read-only GET endpoints, .AsNoTracking() bypasses Change Tracker, cutting query time and RAM by 30-50%.
topics.pitfalls: Calling .AsNoTracking() and then attempting to modify and save with SaveChangesAsync() without re-attaching.
topics.notes:
### EF Core Performance Rules
1. Use .AsNoTracking() on read queries.
2. Project directly to DTOs via .Select(): EF Core generates SQL selecting ONLY those columns!
3. Split queries for multiple includes.

topics.title: EF Core: N+1 Problem, Eager Loading (.Include) & Split Queries
topics.summary: Preventing the N+1 query performance killer, eager loading with .Include(), and avoiding Cartesian product explosion with .AsSplitQuery().
topics.key_intuition: N+1 occurs when querying 100 orders, and accessing order.Customer.Name in a loop triggers 100 separate queries! Fix via Eager Loading (.Include()). Including multiple child collections creates Cartesian explosion; use .AsSplitQuery().
topics.pitfalls: Lazy loading enabled without realization, silently sending hundreds of roundtrips to SQL Server.
topics.notes:
### Cartesian Explosion vs Split Queries
- .Include(o => o.Items).Include(o => o.Logs) returns Items * Logs duplicate rows!
- .AsSplitQuery() executes clean, targeted parallel queries.
topics.code_snippet:
var orders = await _dbContext.Orders
    .AsNoTracking()
    .Include(o => o.Customer)
    .Include(o => o.Items)
    .AsSplitQuery()
    .ToListAsync(ct);

topics.title: API Design: Keyset Pagination, Status Codes & Idempotency
topics.summary: Offset vs Keyset (Cursor) pagination on millions of rows, RFC 7807 ProblemDetails, and Idempotency-Key headers.
topics.key_intuition: OFFSET 1000000 scans and discards 1M rows! Keyset pagination (WHERE Id > @cursor ORDER BY Id LIMIT 20) uses B-tree index in O(1). Idempotency keys prevent double mutation on retry.
topics.pitfalls: Using OFFSET pagination on deep pages; returning 200 OK with error body instead of proper HTTP 4xx/5xx status codes.
topics.notes:
### Keyset Pagination
- Orders by (CreatedAt, Id)
- Query: WHERE CreatedAt < @lastDate OR (CreatedAt = @lastDate AND Id < @lastId)
- Constant O(1) performance at any page depth!

topics.title: JWT Authentication, Claims & Policy-Based Authorization
topics.summary: Configuring JwtBearer in ASP.NET Core, symmetric vs asymmetric keys, claims extraction, and policy requirements.
topics.key_intuition: Authentication verifies token signature and expiration. Policy-based authorization ([Authorize(Policy = "CanRefundOrders")]) allows dynamic condition checks.
topics.pitfalls: Validating tokens without checking issuer or audience; storing secrets in JWT claims (claims are base64 readable!).

topics.title: Apache Kafka: Partitions, Consumer Groups & Offsets
topics.summary: Distributed commit logs, message partitioning key strategy, consumer group scaling limits, and commit offset semantics.
topics.key_intuition: Kafka partitions are append-only sequential files on disk. Ordering guaranteed ONLY within a single partition! Within a Consumer Group, each partition is read by 1 consumer.
topics.pitfalls: Doing heavy synchronous DB work in consumer loop causing heartbeat timeout and rebalancing storms!
topics.notes:
### Offset Commit Semantics
- At-most-once: Commit before processing (loss risk).
- At-least-once (Standard): Process, then commit (requires idempotent consumer!).
- Exactly-once: Kafka transactional producer.

topics.title: NATS Core vs JetStream: Streams, Deduplication & Consumers
topics.summary: High-performance messaging with NATS: Core publish-subscribe vs JetStream persistence, deduplication windows, and durable consumers.
topics.key_intuition: NATS Core is in-memory fire-and-forget (microsecond latency). JetStream adds persistence, stream replay, and message deduplication (Nats-Msg-Id header).
topics.pitfalls: Using NATS Core for critical financial events without JetStream persistence.
topics.notes:
### NATS vs Kafka
- NATS: Single Go binary, microsecond latency, subject-based routing (orders.*.created).
- Kafka: Heavyweight log storage, partitioned big data streams.

topics.title: Dead Letter Queues (DLQ), Retries & Idempotent Consumers
topics.summary: Handling poison pill messages without blocking event streams, exponential backoff retry topics, and consumer deduplication tables.
topics.key_intuition: Network retries guarantee duplicates. Consumers MUST be idempotent: check ProcessedEvents table in DB; if event ID exists, ACK and skip! Repeated failures route to DLQ.
topics.pitfalls: Infinite retry loops blocking the consumer partition; missing unique constraint on MessageId in DB.
topics.notes:
### Idempotent Consumer Flow
1. BEGIN DB Transaction
2. INSERT INTO ProcessedEvents (Id) VALUES (@id) -> If Duplicate: ACK and return
3. Execute business mutation
4. COMMIT
5. ACK message

topics.title: gRPC & Protocol Buffers (Unary vs Streaming RPC)
topics.summary: Binary serialization over HTTP/2, Protobuf contracts, Unary vs Streaming RPC, and RpcException error handling.
topics.key_intuition: gRPC replaces text JSON/HTTP with binary Protobuf over multiplexed HTTP/2. Payloads 7-10x smaller, 5-8x faster serialization. Schema strongly typed via .proto files.
topics.pitfalls: Changing Protobuf field tag numbers (int32 id = 1 -> 2) breaks binary backward compatibility with existing clients.
topics.notes:
### gRPC RPC Types
- Unary: 1 req -> 1 res
- Server Streaming: 1 req -> Stream of res
- Client Streaming: Stream of req -> 1 res
- Bidirectional: Stream <-> Stream

topics.title: BackgroundService & System.Threading.Channels
topics.summary: High-throughput producer-consumer background queues in .NET using thread-safe, lock-free bounded Channels.
topics.key_intuition: System.Threading.Channels provides an ultra-fast, zero-allocation asynchronous producer-consumer channel. Bounded channels provide backpressure (throttles producers if consumers lag).
topics.pitfalls: Using unbounded channels: if producers write faster than workers can process, process runs out of RAM (OOM)!

topics.title: Redis Distributed Caching, Cache-Aside & Stampede Mitigation
topics.summary: In-Memory cache vs Redis, Cache-Aside read/write lifecycle, TTL sliding vs absolute expiration, and thundering herd stampede protection.
topics.key_intuition: In-memory cache is fastest but single-pod local. Redis provides shared distributed state across scaled pods. Protect hot keys from cache stampede using SemaphoreSlim or probabilistic early expiration.
topics.pitfalls: Caching without TTL causing memory leaks; storing large uncompressed JSON strings in Redis.
topics.notes:
### Cache-Aside
1. Check Redis
2. If HIT: return
3. If MISS: load DB, write Redis with TTL, return

topics.title: Structured Logging (Serilog), Correlation IDs & OpenTelemetry
topics.summary: Message templates over string interpolation in Serilog, W3C TraceContext propagation across HTTP and Kafka, and Prometheus metrics.
topics.key_intuition: Never use string interpolation in logs ($"Processing {id}")! Use message templates ("Processing order {OrderId}"): Serilog preserves parameters as searchable JSON attributes. OpenTelemetry standardizes traces.
topics.pitfalls: Logging sensitive customer credentials or credit card numbers (PII/PCI compliance violations).
topics.code_snippet:
Log.Logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
    .ReadFrom.Configuration(config)
    .Enrich.FromLogContext()
    .Enrich.WithCorrelationId()
    .WriteTo.Console(new JsonFormatter())
    .CreateLogger();

topics.title: Unit Testing (xUnit, Moq) & Integration Testing (WebApplicationFactory)
topics.summary: Writing fast unit tests with xUnit & Moq, and spinning up in-memory test servers with WebApplicationFactory for real HTTP end-to-end testing.
topics.key_intuition: Unit tests mock dependencies. Integration tests test real ASP.NET Core pipeline using WebApplicationFactory<Program>: real routing, validation, middleware without network ports.
topics.pitfalls: Testing trivial getters/setters instead of business logic; writing brittle tests that assert private details.
topics.notes:
### WebApplicationFactory
- Spins up TestServer in-memory
- Overrides DI services with TestContainers or In-Memory DB
- Calls real HTTP endpoints via client.GetAsync("/api/...")

topics.title: Multi-Stage Dockerfile for .NET & Container Security
topics.summary: Building lightweight production container images using SDK build stages, chiseled runtime base images, and non-root execution.
topics.key_intuition: Multi-stage Dockerfile: build and publish in Stage 1 with full SDK; copy compiled binaries into minimal runtime image (aspnet:8.0-chiseled). Reduces size from 800MB to ~100MB and eliminates compiler attack surface.
topics.pitfalls: Running container as root in production; baking appsettings secrets into Docker image layers.
topics.notes:
### Multi-Stage Blueprint
Stage 1: FROM dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
Stage 2: FROM dotnet/aspnet:8.0-chiseled AS final
USER app
topics.code_snippet:
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0-chiseled AS final
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/publish .
USER app
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyApp.dll"]

topics.title: CI/CD Pipelines: Azure DevOps & GitHub Actions Automation
topics.summary: Automating build, test verification, container registry push, and automated deployment with secrets and rollbacks.
topics.key_intuition: CI triggers on PR: dotnet build, dotnet test, SonarQube quality gate. CD builds Docker image, pushes to ACR/ECR, updates Kubernetes Helm release. Zero-downtime Blue/Green deployments.
topics.pitfalls: Allowing PRs to merge with failing unit tests; hardcoding connection strings in pipeline YAML files.
topics.notes:
### Pipeline Steps
1. actions/checkout@v4
2. actions/setup-dotnet@v4
3. dotnet test --configuration Release
4. docker/build-push-action@v5

topics.title: Git Mastery: Interactive Rebase, Cherry-Pick & Conflict Resolution
topics.summary: Keeping a clean linear git history using interactive rebase (git rebase -i), safe cherry-picking, and resolving complex 3-way merge conflicts.
topics.key_intuition: git rebase replays commits on top of latest main for a linear commit history. git cherry-pick <hash> applies an isolated hotfix directly into a release branch without merging unready code.
topics.pitfalls: Rebasing a public shared branch that other developers have already pulled (rewrites commit SHA hashes!).
topics.notes:
### Essential Commands
- git rebase -i HEAD~4 (squash WIP commits)
- git pull --rebase origin main
- git cherry-pick <hash>

topics.title: Resilience with Polly: Retries, Exponential Backoff & Circuit Breakers
topics.summary: Protecting microservices from transient network failures and cascading crashes using Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience (Polly v8).
topics.key_intuition: Circuit Breaker monitors failure rates: if > 50% calls fail over 30s, it trips OPEN, failing requests instantly without network traffic. After cooldown, HALF-OPEN tests recovery.
topics.pitfalls: Retrying non-idempotent HTTP POST mutations without idempotency keys; retrying without jitter.

topics.title: CLR Memory Management: GC Generations (0, 1, 2) & LOH
topics.summary: How .NET garbage collection operates: Gen 0 ephemeral allocations, Gen 1 buffer, Gen 2 long-lived objects, and Large Object Heap (LOH) fragmentation.
topics.key_intuition: Generational hypothesis: newly created objects die young! Gen 0 sub-millisecond pauses collect 95% of objects. Objects >= 85,000 bytes go to LOH (not compacted by default). Use ArrayPool<byte>.Shared to reuse buffers.
topics.pitfalls: Allocating large byte arrays repeatedly in Web API request handlers, triggering frequent full Gen 2 / LOH blocking GC pauses.
topics.notes:
### Memory Optimization Rules
1. Use ArrayPool<T>.Shared.Rent(size) and return in finally.
2. Use Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<char> to slice strings without heap allocations.
3. Profile using dotnet-gcdump to track memory leaks.

topics.title: Rate Limiting Middleware in .NET 7/8
topics.summary: Built-in ASP.NET Core rate limiting algorithms (Token Bucket, Sliding Window, Fixed Window) and custom client partitioners.
topics.key_intuition: Built-in Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting eliminates 3rd-party dependencies. Partition rate limits dynamically by client IP or authenticated user ID. Return HTTP 429 with Retry-After.
topics.pitfalls: Applying a single global rate limit across all clients, allowing one rogue client to exhaust the budget for all legitimate users.
topics.notes:
### Built-in .NET 8 Rate Limiter
- FixedWindowLimiter
- SlidingWindowLimiter
- TokenBucketLimiter (burst friendly)
- ConcurrencyLimiter

topics.title: Thread Safety: SemaphoreSlim, Interlocked & Concurrent Collections
topics.summary: Safe multi-threaded code in backend services: why you cannot use lock with await, SemaphoreSlim for async throttling, and atomic Interlocked operations.
topics.key_intuition: YOU CANNOT await INSIDE A C# lock BLOCK! To synchronize asynchronous operations, use SemaphoreSlim(1, 1) with await semaphore.WaitAsync(). For counters, use Interlocked.Increment() for lock-free atomics.
topics.pitfalls: Deadlocks when acquiring multiple semaphores in different orders across services; forgetting semaphore.Release() in a finally block.

topics.title: Configuration Management (IOptions) & Feature Flags
topics.summary: Strongly typed configuration using IOptions / IOptionsSnapshot / IOptionsMonitor, and zero-downtime dark launches with Microsoft.FeatureManagement.
topics.key_intuition: Never read _config["MyKey"] directly. Bind to POCO classes using IOptions<T> (Singleton), IOptionsSnapshot<T> (scoped per request), or IOptionsMonitor<T> (hot-reload notifications). Feature flags decouple deployment from release.
topics.pitfalls: Using IOptionsSnapshot inside a Singleton service (captive dependency!); storing unencrypted secrets in git.
topics.notes:
### IOptions Flavor Guide
- IOptions<T>: Singleton, registered at startup.
- IOptionsSnapshot<T>: Scoped, computed per request.
- IOptionsMonitor<T>: Singleton with hot reload callbacks.

topics.title: Tokens, Context Windows & Cost Math
topics.summary: How text becomes tokens, what the context window limits, and how to estimate latency and cost per request.
topics.key_intuition: Models read and bill in tokens (about 4 English characters, roughly 0.75 words). Cost = input_tokens x input_price + output_tokens x output_price, and output tokens cost several times more. Chat history is re-sent every turn, so cost per turn grows with conversation length.
topics.pitfalls: Assuming the advertised context size is usable quality-wise (long contexts degrade recall in the middle); forgetting that tool results and system prompts also count; not setting max_tokens.
topics.notes:
### Tokens, Context Windows & Cost Math
- Category: 1. LLM Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Easy

### Tokens & Context
- Tokenizer is model-specific (BPE variants); count with the provider tokenizer, never by characters.
- Context window = input + output tokens combined.
- Prefill (reading the prompt) is fast and parallel; decode (generating) is sequential, so latency ~ TTFT + output_tokens x time_per_token.
- Budget every request: system prompt + history + retrieved chunks + tool results + reserved output.
- Trim strategies: sliding window, summarise old turns, drop stale tool results.

### Back-of-envelope
10k input + 1k output tokens at $3/M in and $15/M out = $0.03 + $0.015 = $0.045 per call. At 100k calls/day that is $4,500/day, which is why caching and routing matter.

topics.title: How LLMs Work: Transformers, Attention & KV Cache
topics.summary: Mental model of autoregressive transformer inference: attention, next-token prediction, prefill vs decode, KV cache.
topics.key_intuition: An LLM predicts one next token at a time from a probability distribution over the vocabulary. Self-attention lets each token weigh every earlier token: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) V. The KV cache stores past keys/values so each new token does not recompute the whole prompt.
topics.pitfalls: Believing the model "looks things up" or "knows" facts reliably; treating outputs as deterministic; ignoring that attention cost grows with context length.
topics.notes:
### How LLMs Work: Transformers, Attention & KV Cache
- Category: 1. LLM Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Key ideas for interviews
- Autoregressive: output token is appended to input, repeat until stop token.
- Attention is O(n^2) in sequence length (before optimisations like FlashAttention).
- KV cache trades GPU memory for speed; it is why long contexts and many concurrent users are memory-bound.
- Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; prefill is compute-bound.
- Hallucination is a consequence of next-token likelihood without grounding, so grounding (RAG, tools) is the fix, not "better prompts" alone.
- Training stages: pre-training -> supervised fine-tuning -> preference tuning (RLHF/DPO) -> optional reasoning RL.

topics.title: Sampling: Temperature, Top-p, Top-k & Stop Sequences
topics.summary: Controlling randomness and termination of generation, and when to use which setting.
topics.key_intuition: Temperature rescales logits before softmax: low = peaked/predictable, high = diverse. Top-p (nucleus) keeps the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p; top-k keeps the k most likely. Use low temperature for extraction, classification and tool calls; higher for brainstorming.
topics.pitfalls: Expecting temperature 0 to be fully deterministic (batching and floating-point make it only mostly stable); tuning temperature and top-p together aggressively; some reasoning models ignore or fix these parameters.
topics.notes:
### Sampling: Temperature, Top-p, Top-k & Stop Sequences
- Category: 1. LLM Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Easy

### Practical defaults
- Extraction / JSON / tool calling: temperature 0 to 0.2
- Chat / summarisation: 0.3 to 0.7
- Creative: 0.8+
- Stop sequences end generation early and save tokens.
- Seed parameters (where supported) improve reproducibility but are not a guarantee.
- Always pin the model version in production so behaviour does not shift under you.

topics.title: Model Selection: Frontier vs Small vs Open-Weight
topics.summary: Choosing models by quality, latency, cost, context size, modality, privacy and licensing.
topics.key_intuition: Use the cheapest model that passes your evals. Route easy/high-volume steps (classification, extraction, routing) to small fast models and reserve frontier or reasoning models for hard planning and synthesis.
topics.pitfalls: Picking by leaderboard instead of your own eval set; hard-coding a single vendor; ignoring data residency and retention policy.
topics.notes:
### Model Selection: Frontier vs Small vs Open-Weight
- Category: 1. LLM Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Decision matrix
- Quality-critical reasoning/coding: frontier or reasoning models.
- High-volume, simple: small models (cost and latency 10x lower).
- Privacy / on-prem / offline: open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Mistral families) via Ollama, vLLM.
- Multimodal: check vision/audio support and image token costs.
- Always abstract the provider (IChatClient in .NET, AI SDK providers in TS) so swapping is a config change.
- Re-run evals on every model upgrade.

topics.title: Structured Outputs & JSON Schema
topics.summary: Forcing model output into a validated schema so backend code can consume it safely.
topics.key_intuition: Free text is for humans; programs need typed data. Use provider structured-output / JSON-schema modes (constrained decoding) and still validate on your side with Zod or System.Text.Json, because a valid shape does not mean valid meaning.
topics.pitfalls: Parsing JSON out of prose with regex; trusting enum values without validation; deeply nested schemas that hurt accuracy; no retry-with-error-feedback path.
topics.notes:
### Structured Outputs & JSON Schema
- Category: 1. LLM Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Pattern
1. Define schema (Zod / C# record).
2. Ask provider for structured output with that schema.
3. Validate; on failure, send the validation error back once or twice, then fail.
4. Add business validation (ranges, IDs exist in DB).

Keep schemas flat, use descriptions on fields (the model reads them), prefer enums over free strings.

topics.title: Embeddings & Semantic Similarity
topics.summary: Turning text into vectors so meaning can be compared with cosine similarity; the foundation of RAG, search and memory.
topics.key_intuition: An embedding model maps text to a fixed-length vector where similar meaning means small angle. Cosine similarity = dot(a,b)/(|a||b|); with normalised vectors it equals the dot product.
topics.pitfalls: Mixing embedding models between indexing and querying; not re-indexing after changing models; embedding huge chunks (diluted meaning); assuming semantic search handles exact IDs or rare keywords well.
topics.notes:
### Embeddings & Semantic Similarity
- Category: 1. LLM Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Facts to remember
- Dimensions (e.g. 384, 768, 1536, 3072) affect storage and speed; some models support truncation (Matryoshka).
- Store model name + version with every vector.
- Query and document may need different prefixes/instructions for some models.
- Embeddings are not secret: they can leak information about source text, so apply the same access control as the source.
- Use for: semantic search, dedup, clustering, classification, routing, memory retrieval.

topics.title: System Prompts, Roles & Instruction Hierarchy
topics.summary: Structuring system, developer and user messages so behaviour is stable and instructions are prioritised correctly.
topics.key_intuition: The system prompt defines role, rules, tools policy and output format; user content is untrusted data. Be explicit, specific and positive ("do X") and give the model an out ("if unsure say so").
topics.pitfalls: Putting secrets in the system prompt (it can leak); contradictory rules; giant prompts with no structure; mixing instructions with untrusted retrieved text.
topics.notes:
### System Prompts, Roles & Instruction Hierarchy
- Category: 2. Prompt & Context Engineering
- Difficulty: Easy

### Prompt skeleton
1. Role & goal
2. Context / domain facts
3. Rules & constraints
4. Tool-use guidance
5. Output format (schema or template)
6. Examples

Use XML-style or markdown delimiters to separate sections and untrusted data (<document>...</document>). Keep prompts in files with version control, not scattered in code.

topics.title: Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought & Reasoning Models
topics.summary: Techniques that improve accuracy: examples, step-by-step reasoning, and when dedicated reasoning models make them unnecessary.
topics.key_intuition: Few-shot examples teach format and edge cases better than prose. Chain-of-thought gives the model room to compute intermediate steps. Reasoning models do this internally, so over-prescribing steps can hurt.
topics.pitfalls: Examples that are all similar (model copies them); leaking test cases into prompts; paying for long reasoning on trivial tasks; relying on displayed reasoning as a faithful explanation.
topics.notes:
### Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought & Reasoning Models
- Category: 2. Prompt & Context Engineering
- Difficulty: Medium

### Guidance
- 3 to 5 diverse, realistic examples covering edge cases and a refusal/unknown case.
- For standard models: "think step by step" on multi-step logic.
- For reasoning models: state the goal and constraints, let them think; control cost via reasoning-effort settings.
- Self-consistency: sample N answers and take the majority for high-stakes classification.
- Always measure with an eval set, not by feel.

topics.title: Context Engineering for Agents
topics.summary: Curating exactly what goes into the context window each step: instructions, tools, retrieved data, history, memory.
topics.key_intuition: Context is a scarce resource with diminishing returns. Give the smallest set of high-signal tokens that makes the next step succeed: just-in-time retrieval, compaction of old history, structured notes outside the window, and sub-agents with clean contexts.
topics.pitfalls: Dumping all tools and documents in every call; letting tool outputs grow unbounded; stale or contradictory facts left in history; poisoning the context with a failed attempt and never pruning it.
topics.notes:
### Context Engineering for Agents
- Category: 2. Prompt & Context Engineering
- Difficulty: Hard

### Techniques
- Compaction: summarise old turns, keep decisions and open TODOs.
- Note-taking: agent writes progress to a file/DB and reads it back (survives context resets).
- Just-in-time retrieval: hold identifiers (paths, URLs, IDs) and load content only when needed.
- Tool-result clearing: drop old raw outputs once consumed.
- Sub-agents: delegate a search/analysis task and return only a condensed result.
- Order matters: static content first (enables prompt caching), volatile content last.

topics.title: Prompt Templates, Versioning & Regression Testing
topics.summary: Treating prompts as code: templates, versions, review, and automated regression checks against an eval set.
topics.key_intuition: A prompt change is a behaviour change. Store prompts in source control with an ID/version, log the version on every request, and run the eval suite in CI before shipping.
topics.pitfalls: Editing prompts directly in production dashboards with no history; no way to correlate a bad answer to a prompt version; fixing one failure and silently breaking five others.
topics.notes:
### Prompt Templates, Versioning & Regression Testing
- Category: 2. Prompt & Context Engineering
- Difficulty: Medium

### Workflow
1. Prompt file with variables ({{customer_name}}).
2. Unit evals: representative inputs + assertions (schema valid, contains/forbids phrases, judge score).
3. CI gate: score must not regress beyond threshold.
4. Canary/A-B new prompt on a slice of traffic.
5. Log prompt_version, model, tokens, latency per request.

topics.title: RAG Architecture: Ingestion to Generation
topics.summary: End-to-end Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline: load, chunk, embed, index, retrieve, rerank, generate, cite.
topics.key_intuition: RAG grounds the model in your data at query time instead of baking knowledge into weights. Quality is mostly determined by retrieval: if the right chunk is not retrieved, no prompt can save the answer.
topics.pitfalls: Evaluating only the final answer (cannot tell retrieval vs generation failure); no citations; ignoring document permissions; stale index with no refresh pipeline.
topics.notes:
### RAG Architecture: Ingestion to Generation
- Category: 3. RAG & Vector Search
- Difficulty: Medium

### Pipeline
- Ingestion: parse (PDF/HTML/MD), clean, chunk, embed, upsert with metadata (source, ACL, version, updated_at).
- Query: rewrite -> embed -> retrieve top-k -> (hybrid + rerank) -> assemble context -> generate with citations.
- Enforce access control at retrieval (metadata filter by user/tenant), never after generation.
- Instruct: "Answer only from the context; if missing say you do not know."
- Keep an incremental re-index job keyed by content hash.

topics.title: Chunking Strategies & Metadata
topics.summary: Splitting documents into retrievable units that preserve meaning, with metadata for filtering and citation.
topics.key_intuition: Chunks should be self-contained answers. Structure-aware splitting (by heading/section/function) beats fixed-size splitting; small chunks retrieve precisely, large chunks give context, so parent-child retrieval gives both.
topics.pitfalls: Cutting tables/code mid-way; no overlap at boundaries; losing the heading context (prepend the title path to each chunk); one chunk size for all document types.
topics.notes:
### Chunking Strategies & Metadata
- Category: 3. RAG & Vector Search
- Difficulty: Medium

### Starting points
- 200 to 800 tokens, 10 to 20% overlap for prose.
- Split on headings first, then paragraphs, then sentences.
- Code: chunk by function/class; keep file path and language in metadata.
- Contextual retrieval: prepend a short LLM-generated situating sentence to each chunk before embedding.
- Metadata: source URL, title path, page, tenant_id, ACL, doc_version, created/updated.

topics.title: Vector Databases, ANN Indexes & pgvector
topics.summary: Approximate nearest neighbour search (HNSW, IVF), distance metrics, and choosing between pgvector and dedicated vector stores.
topics.key_intuition: Exact search is O(n); ANN indexes trade a little recall for big speed. HNSW is a layered proximity graph (tune m, ef_construction, ef_search). IVF clusters vectors and probes a few lists. For most apps already on Postgres, pgvector is enough.
topics.pitfalls: Building an index before loading data (IVFFlat needs data for clustering); not applying metadata filters efficiently (post-filtering kills recall); ignoring memory footprint of HNSW.
topics.notes:
### Vector Databases, ANN Indexes & pgvector
- Category: 3. RAG & Vector Search
- Difficulty: Medium

### pgvector operators
- <-> L2 distance, <=> cosine distance, <#> negative inner product.
- Index: CREATE INDEX ON docs USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
- Tune at query time: SET hnsw.ef_search = 100;

### Choosing
- pgvector: transactional joins, one system, up to millions of vectors.
- Dedicated (Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus, Azure AI Search): very large scale, built-in hybrid, managed ops.

topics.title: Hybrid Search, RRF & Reranking
topics.summary: Combining keyword (BM25) and vector search, fusing ranks, and re-scoring with a cross-encoder reranker.
topics.key_intuition: Vectors capture meaning but miss exact tokens (error codes, SKUs); BM25 does the opposite. Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges both lists: score = sum of 1/(k + rank), typically k = 60. A cross-encoder reranker then re-scores the top 50 to 100 candidates down to the best 5 to 10.
topics.pitfalls: Adding a reranker without measuring recall@k first; sending too many chunks to the LLM; ignoring latency of the rerank step.
topics.notes:
### Hybrid Search, RRF & Reranking
- Category: 3. RAG & Vector Search
- Difficulty: Hard

### Metrics
- Retrieval: recall@k, precision@k, MRR, nDCG.
- Build a labelled set of (question -> relevant chunk ids) from real queries.

### Pipeline
BM25 top 50 + vector top 50 -> RRF -> reranker top 8 -> LLM.

topics.title: Advanced RAG: Query Rewriting, HyDE, Agentic RAG & GraphRAG
topics.summary: Techniques beyond naive RAG for ambiguous, multi-hop and global questions.
topics.key_intuition: Rewrite the user question into good search queries (decompose, expand, use chat history). HyDE embeds a hypothetical answer. Agentic RAG lets the model decide when and what to retrieve, iterating until it has enough. GraphRAG builds an entity graph for corpus-wide questions.
topics.pitfalls: Multiplying LLM calls (latency/cost) for questions that simple retrieval handles; letting the agent loop without a step budget; building a graph when the corpus does not need it.
topics.notes:
### Advanced RAG: Query Rewriting, HyDE, Agentic RAG & GraphRAG
- Category: 3. RAG & Vector Search
- Difficulty: Hard

### When to use
- Follow-up questions: condense with history.
- Multi-hop ("compare A and B"): decompose into sub-queries, retrieve each, synthesise.
- Low retrieval confidence: fallback query rewrite, then admit uncertainty.
- Global/summary questions: hierarchical summaries or GraphRAG.
- Expose retrieval as a tool (search_docs) so the agent can call it multiple times.

topics.title: Evaluating RAG: Faithfulness, Relevance & Retrieval Quality
topics.summary: Measuring retrieval and generation separately so failures can be diagnosed and fixed.
topics.key_intuition: Split the problem: did we retrieve the right context (context recall/precision) and did the answer stay grounded in it (faithfulness) and address the question (answer relevance)?
topics.pitfalls: Using only an LLM judge with no human calibration; test sets written by the same model that builds the system; no tracking over time.
topics.notes:
### Evaluating RAG: Faithfulness, Relevance & Retrieval Quality
- Category: 3. RAG & Vector Search
- Difficulty: Hard

### Metrics
- Retrieval: recall@k, MRR, nDCG, context precision/recall.
- Generation: faithfulness/groundedness, answer relevance, citation correctness, refusal correctness when no answer exists.
- Tools: Ragas, DeepEval, Promptfoo, LangSmith/Langfuse datasets.
- Build the golden set from real user questions plus synthetic ones; include unanswerable and adversarial cases.

topics.title: Workflows vs Agents: Choosing the Right Pattern
topics.summary: Predefined LLM workflows (chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) versus autonomous agents.
topics.key_intuition: Workflows orchestrate LLMs through code paths you define; agents let the LLM direct its own process and tool use. Start with the simplest thing (a single call with retrieval), add workflow structure for reliability, and use a true agent only when the path cannot be predicted.
topics.pitfalls: Reaching for an autonomous agent for a fixed process; no stop conditions; framework abstractions that hide prompts and make debugging impossible.
topics.notes:
### Workflows vs Agents: Choosing the Right Pattern
- Category: 4. Agent Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Five workflow patterns
1. Prompt chaining: fixed sequence with gates between steps.
2. Routing: classify input then dispatch to a specialised path or model.
3. Parallelisation: sectioning independent subtasks, or voting for confidence.
4. Orchestrator-workers: a lead model splits dynamic subtasks and merges results.
5. Evaluator-optimizer: generate, critique, refine loop.

Agents add: tool use in a loop, environment feedback, and a stopping condition (done, max steps, budget, human checkpoint).

topics.title: The Agent Loop & ReAct
topics.summary: The core think-act-observe loop that powers tool-using agents, with proper termination and budgets.
topics.key_intuition: Loop: send messages + tool definitions -> model returns text or tool calls -> run tools -> append results -> repeat until the model returns a final answer or a limit is hit. ReAct is this pattern with explicit reasoning between actions.
topics.pitfalls: No max-iterations or token/cost budget; infinite retry of a failing tool; swallowing tool errors instead of returning them to the model; unbounded context growth.
topics.notes:
### The Agent Loop & ReAct
- Category: 4. Agent Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Minimum viable agent
- Tools described by JSON schema.
- Loop with max_steps (e.g. 10 to 25), cost cap and timeout.
- Tool errors returned as tool_result with is_error so the model can adapt.
- Detect repeated identical calls (loop detection).
- Persist every step for tracing and replay.

topics.title: Tool / Function Calling Design
topics.summary: Designing tool schemas, descriptions and results so models call them correctly and safely.
topics.key_intuition: Tools are an API for the model. Clear names, precise descriptions with when-to-use guidance, strongly-typed parameters, and concise, informative results make the difference between a flaky and a reliable agent.
topics.pitfalls: Too many overlapping tools; vague descriptions; returning huge raw payloads; tools with side effects that are not idempotent; trusting model-provided arguments without validation.
topics.notes:
### Tool / Function Calling Design
- Category: 4. Agent Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Medium

### Design rules
- Few, well-scoped tools; merge near-duplicates.
- Description says what, when, and when NOT to use.
- Validate arguments server-side (schema + authorisation as the end user, not as the agent).
- Return only what is needed, with stable IDs the model can pass to the next tool.
- Make writes idempotent (idempotency key) and support dry-run/confirm for destructive ones.
- Support parallel tool calls when calls are independent.

topics.title: Planning, Reflection & Self-Correction
topics.summary: Letting agents plan multi-step work, verify results, and recover from errors.
topics.key_intuition: Explicit plans (a todo list the agent updates) keep long tasks on track. Reflection steps check output against requirements using real signals (tests, schema validation, search results) rather than the model re-reading its own answer.
topics.pitfalls: Self-critique without external ground truth just rubber-stamps errors; over-planning for simple tasks; plans that never get updated.
topics.notes:
### Planning, Reflection & Self-Correction
- Category: 4. Agent Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Hard

### Patterns
- Plan-and-execute: planner produces steps, executor runs them, replan on failure.
- Verifier: run tests/linters/validators and feed failures back.
- Reflexion: store lessons from failed attempts in memory for the next try.
- Cap retries and escalate to a human when blocked.

topics.title: Agent Memory: Short-Term, Long-Term & Episodic
topics.summary: Persisting useful state across steps and sessions without bloating the context window.
topics.key_intuition: Short-term memory is the context window. Long-term memory is external: facts/preferences (semantic), past interactions (episodic), and learned procedures (procedural), retrieved when relevant.
topics.pitfalls: Storing everything (noise); no expiry or correction of wrong memories; leaking one user's memory to another; treating retrieved memory as trusted instructions.
topics.notes:
### Agent Memory: Short-Term, Long-Term & Episodic
- Category: 4. Agent Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Hard

### Implementation
- Summarise conversation incrementally; store summary + key facts.
- Extract durable facts ("prefers TypeScript") with an LLM step, dedupe, store in DB/vector index keyed by user.
- Retrieve top relevant memories per turn and place them in a clearly-labelled section.
- Give users view/edit/delete controls; honour privacy rules.
- Scope strictly by tenant and user.

topics.title: Multi-Agent Systems: Supervisor, Handoffs & Sub-Agents
topics.summary: Splitting work across specialised agents and coordinating them.
topics.key_intuition: Multiple agents help when subtasks are parallel, need different tools/permissions, or would overflow one context. They cost more tokens and add coordination failures, so use one agent until you have evidence it is not enough.
topics.pitfalls: Agents talking in circles; vague hand-off contracts; duplicated work; no single owner of the final answer; debugging without traces.
topics.notes:
### Multi-Agent Systems: Supervisor, Handoffs & Sub-Agents
- Category: 4. Agent Fundamentals
- Difficulty: Hard

### Topologies
- Supervisor/orchestrator with worker agents.
- Hand-off (swarm): agent transfers control with context to another.
- Parallel researchers + synthesiser.
- Critic/reviewer pair.

### Rules
- Each sub-agent gets a precise brief: objective, output format, tool guidance, boundaries.
- Return condensed results to the lead, not full transcripts.
- Trace every agent run under one parent trace ID.

topics.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
topics.summary: Open protocol for connecting AI applications to tools, data and prompts through standard servers.
topics.key_intuition: MCP is like USB-C for AI tools: build one server and any MCP-capable client (IDE, desktop assistant, your own agent) can use it. It uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (local) or Streamable HTTP (remote).
topics.pitfalls: Installing untrusted MCP servers (they run code and feed content into the model); over-broad tool permissions; exposing hundreds of tools and flooding the context; skipping auth on remote servers.
topics.notes:
### Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Category: 5. Tools, MCP & Frameworks
- Difficulty: Medium

### Concepts
- Server primitives: tools (actions), resources (readable data), prompts (templates).
- Client features: sampling, roots, elicitation.
- Transports: stdio for local, Streamable HTTP for remote; remote servers should use OAuth-based authorisation.
- SDKs: TypeScript, Python, C# (official), Java, Kotlin.
- Treat tool descriptions and outputs as untrusted input (prompt-injection surface).

topics.title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) & Interoperability
topics.summary: Protocols for agents built on different stacks to discover each other and collaborate.
topics.key_intuition: MCP connects an agent to tools and data; A2A connects agents to other agents. Agents publish an Agent Card describing skills and endpoints, then exchange tasks and messages over HTTP.
topics.pitfalls: Assuming remote agents are trustworthy; ignoring authentication and task-level authorisation; chaining agents with no timeouts.
topics.notes:
### Agent-to-Agent (A2A) & Interoperability
- Category: 5. Tools, MCP & Frameworks
- Difficulty: Hard

### Mental model
- MCP = vertical (agent <-> tools).
- A2A = horizontal (agent <-> agent).
- Key objects: Agent Card (capabilities), Task (long-running unit with lifecycle), Message/Artifact.
- Use when crossing team/vendor boundaries; inside one codebase plain function calls or in-process orchestration are simpler.

topics.title: LangGraph: Stateful Agent Graphs, Checkpoints & Human-in-the-Loop
topics.summary: Modelling agents as graphs of nodes with shared state, persistence and interrupts.
topics.key_intuition: A graph makes control flow explicit: nodes (LLM call, tool, function), edges (conditional routing), and a typed state. A checkpointer saves state after each step so runs can resume, be inspected, rewound, or paused for human approval.
topics.pitfalls: Using a framework when a 30-line loop would do; hiding prompts behind abstractions; not persisting checkpoints in production (in-memory only).
topics.notes:
### LangGraph: Stateful Agent Graphs, Checkpoints & Human-in-the-Loop
- Category: 5. Tools, MCP & Frameworks
- Difficulty: Hard

### Why graphs
- Deterministic structure around non-deterministic LLM steps.
- Interrupts: pause before a sensitive tool call, wait for approval, then resume.
- Time travel/debugging via checkpoints.
- Streaming of intermediate state to the UI.

Alternatives: OpenAI Agents SDK, Mastra, Vercel AI SDK agents, Microsoft Agent Framework. Learn one deeply, keep the concepts portable.

topics.title: .NET AI Stack: Microsoft.Extensions.AI & Agent Framework
topics.summary: Building LLM features in C#: IChatClient, IEmbeddingGenerator, function invocation, and agent orchestration for .NET backends.
topics.key_intuition: Microsoft.Extensions.AI gives provider-agnostic abstractions (IChatClient, IEmbeddingGenerator) with middleware (function invocation, caching, logging, OpenTelemetry). Higher-level agent orchestration is provided by Microsoft Agent Framework (the evolution of Semantic Kernel and AutoGen ideas).
topics.pitfalls: Binding business code to one vendor SDK; registering clients as singletons without considering options per request; forgetting cancellation tokens on streaming calls.
topics.notes:
### .NET AI Stack: Microsoft.Extensions.AI & Agent Framework
- Category: 5. Tools, MCP & Frameworks
- Difficulty: Medium

### Key pieces
- IChatClient: GetResponseAsync / GetStreamingResponseAsync.
- ChatClientBuilder pipeline: UseFunctionInvocation(), UseOpenTelemetry(), UseDistributedCache(), UseLogging().
- AIFunctionFactory.Create(method) turns a C# method into a tool.
- DI registration: services.AddChatClient(...).
- Use Azure OpenAI / OpenAI / Ollama / GitHub Models interchangeably behind the interface.
- Pair with pgvector or Azure AI Search for RAG, and Semantic Kernel/Agent Framework for multi-step agents.

topics.title: Vercel AI SDK & TypeScript Agent SDKs
topics.summary: TypeScript toolkit for streaming chat, tool calling, structured output and agents in Next.js apps.
topics.key_intuition: The AI SDK normalises providers behind generateText/streamText/generateObject, with a useChat hook on the client and typed tools on the server. Same concepts exist in OpenAI Agents SDK, Mastra and LangChain.js.
topics.pitfalls: Calling provider keys from the browser; not setting maxDuration on serverless routes; not handling abort/disconnect; coupling UI message format to one provider.
topics.notes:
### Vercel AI SDK & TypeScript Agent SDKs
- Category: 5. Tools, MCP & Frameworks
- Difficulty: Medium

### Server route sketch
- streamText({ model, system, messages, tools, stopWhen }) returns a stream.
- Return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse() to the client.
- Client uses useChat to render parts (text, tool calls, reasoning).
- Multi-step tool loops are controlled by stop conditions (step count).
- Keep API keys server-side only; add auth and rate limits on the route.

topics.title: Streaming Responses: SSE, Backpressure & Cancellation
topics.summary: Delivering tokens to the browser as they are generated, and handling disconnects and proxies correctly.
topics.key_intuition: Time-to-first-token is what users feel. Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream) are the simplest one-way streaming transport; propagate client aborts to the model call so you stop paying for tokens nobody reads.
topics.pitfalls: Reverse proxies buffering the stream (disable buffering, e.g. nginx proxy_buffering off); no heartbeat; ignoring request abort signals; swallowing mid-stream errors.
topics.notes:
### Streaming Responses: SSE, Backpressure & Cancellation
- Category: 6. Full-Stack AI Apps
- Difficulty: Medium

### Checklist
- Headers: Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache, Connection keep-alive.
- Forward AbortSignal to the LLM client.
- Emit structured events (text-delta, tool-call, error, done).
- Retry/resume: include event ids so clients can reconnect.
- ASP.NET Core: return IAsyncEnumerable<T> from a minimal API or use TypedResults.ServerSentEvents.
- WebSockets only if you need bidirectional realtime (voice, collaborative).

topics.title: Building the Chat UI: useChat, Tool Rendering & Generative UI
topics.summary: Frontend patterns for AI products: streaming messages, tool-call states, optimistic UI, citations, stop/regenerate.
topics.key_intuition: Treat a message as a list of typed parts (text, reasoning, tool call, source). Render each part with its own component, show tool progress, and let the model choose a UI component by calling a tool that maps to a React component.
topics.pitfalls: Re-rendering the whole transcript on every token; rendering model-produced HTML unsanitised (XSS); no stop button; losing history on refresh.
topics.notes:
### Building the Chat UI: useChat, Tool Rendering & Generative UI
- Category: 6. Full-Stack AI Apps
- Difficulty: Medium

### UX essentials
- Stop, retry, edit-and-resubmit, copy.
- Show sources/citations with links back to the document chunk.
- Show agent steps ("Searching orders...") for transparency.
- Markdown render with a sanitiser; syntax highlighting for code.
- Persist conversations server-side; paginate long histories.
- Human approval cards for sensitive tool calls.
- Accessibility: aria-live for streamed text, keyboard shortcuts.

topics.title: LLM Backends in .NET / Node: API Design, Auth & Multi-Tenancy
topics.summary: Structuring a production API around LLM calls: auth, tenant isolation, per-user context, request limits and error mapping.
topics.key_intuition: The LLM is just another unreliable downstream dependency. Wrap it behind a service interface, run tools with the end user's identity, and isolate tenants at the data layer (never rely on the prompt to enforce isolation).
topics.pitfalls: Running tools with a powerful service account; passing user identity only in the prompt; no timeouts; leaking provider error messages to clients.
topics.notes:
### LLM Backends in .NET / Node: API Design, Auth & Multi-Tenancy
- Category: 6. Full-Stack AI Apps
- Difficulty: Medium

### Layers
1. Controller / minimal API: auth (JWT), validation, rate limit.
2. Application service: builds messages, selects model, applies budgets.
3. Tool layer: authorises every call against the current user.
4. Provider layer: IChatClient with Polly resilience, retries with jitter, circuit breaker.
5. Persistence: conversations, messages, usage records, feedback.

Map provider errors (429, 5xx, content filter) to clean API responses and fallbacks.

topics.title: Long-Running Agent Jobs: Queues, Durable Execution & Resumability
topics.summary: Running multi-minute agent tasks reliably outside the request/response cycle.
topics.key_intuition: Serverless request timeouts and flaky networks kill long agent runs. Enqueue the job, run it in a worker with checkpointing after every step, and stream progress to the UI via SSE or polling.
topics.pitfalls: Non-idempotent tools re-executed on retry; losing state when a worker restarts; no cancellation; unbounded cost per job.
topics.notes:
### Long-Running Agent Jobs: Queues, Durable Execution & Resumability
- Category: 6. Full-Stack AI Apps
- Difficulty: Hard

### Building blocks
- Queue + worker: BackgroundService with System.Threading.Channels, Hangfire, Azure Service Bus; or Inngest, Temporal, Azure Durable Functions in TS/.NET.
- Persist run state (steps, tool results) so a retry replays instead of redoing side effects.
- Job API: POST /runs -> 202 + runId; GET /runs/{id}; SSE /runs/{id}/events; DELETE to cancel.
- Per-run budgets: max steps, tokens, wall-clock.

topics.title: Cost & Latency Control: Caching, Routing, Rate Limits & Budgets
topics.summary: Keeping AI features fast and affordable at scale.
topics.key_intuition: Biggest wins in order: shorter prompts, prompt caching (stable prefix first), model routing, response/semantic caching, then batch APIs for offline work. Enforce per-user and per-tenant token budgets to prevent runaway bills.
topics.pitfalls: Semantic cache returning another user's answer; caching responses that depend on private data; no per-user quota; ignoring output-length limits.
topics.notes:
### Cost & Latency Control: Caching, Routing, Rate Limits & Budgets
- Category: 6. Full-Stack AI Apps
- Difficulty: Medium

### Toolbox
- Provider prompt caching: place system prompt and static docs at the start; vary the end.
- Exact-match cache for deterministic requests (hash of prompt+params).
- Semantic cache with a high similarity threshold and tenant scoping.
- Router: small model first, escalate on low confidence.
- Batch APIs (typically ~50% cheaper) for evals, backfills, enrichment.
- Rate limiting: token-bucket per user/tenant (ASP.NET Core RateLimiter) measured in tokens, not only requests.
- Dashboards: cost per user, per feature, per model.

topics.title: Building Eval Datasets & LLM-as-Judge
topics.summary: Creating repeatable evaluations for non-deterministic systems, using code graders, LLM judges and human review.
topics.key_intuition: You cannot improve what you cannot measure. Start with 50 to 200 real examples, write the cheapest reliable grader for each (exact match, schema, regex, unit test), and use an LLM judge with a rubric only where needed, calibrated against human labels.
topics.pitfalls: Judge biases (position, verbosity, self-preference); vague rubrics; overfitting prompts to the eval set; never refreshing the set with production failures.
topics.notes:
### Building Eval Datasets & LLM-as-Judge
- Category: 7. Evals & Observability
- Difficulty: Hard

### Process
1. Collect cases from logs, support tickets and edge cases.
2. Define success criteria per case.
3. Graders: deterministic first, then rubric-based LLM judge (pairwise comparison reduces bias; randomise order).
4. Track score per category, not just overall.
5. Run in CI; keep a held-out set.
6. Add every production bug as a new case.

Tools: Promptfoo, Braintrust, LangSmith, Langfuse, DeepEval, Inspect.

topics.title: Tracing & Observability with OpenTelemetry GenAI
