topics.summary: Seeing inside prompts, tool calls, tokens, latency and cost for every request.
topics.key_intuition: Agents are debugged by reading traces. Capture one trace per user request with spans for each LLM call and tool call, including model, prompt version, token counts, latency, and errors. OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions standardise attribute names (gen_ai.*).
topics.pitfalls: Logging raw prompts containing PII without redaction; no correlation between traces and user feedback; sampling away the failing runs.
topics.notes:
### Tracing & Observability with OpenTelemetry GenAI
- Category: 7. Evals & Observability
- Difficulty: Medium

### What to record
- gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens, finish reason.
- Prompt version, tool names + arguments + latency + status.
- User feedback (thumbs) linked to trace id.
- Cost per trace computed from token usage.

Backends: Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize Phoenix, Azure Monitor/Application Insights, Grafana/Tempo. In .NET: ChatClientBuilder.UseOpenTelemetry().

topics.title: Evaluating Agents: Trajectories, Tool Accuracy & Reliability
topics.summary: Metrics for multi-step agents beyond final-answer quality.
topics.key_intuition: Agents can reach the right answer the wrong way (or fail only occasionally). Measure task success in a sandboxed environment, check tool-call correctness and arguments, count steps/cost, and run each case multiple times (pass^k) to measure consistency.
topics.pitfalls: Testing against live production systems with side effects; single-run results on non-deterministic agents; ignoring cost and step count regressions.
topics.notes:
### Evaluating Agents: Trajectories, Tool Accuracy & Reliability
- Category: 7. Evals & Observability
- Difficulty: Hard

### Metrics
- Task success rate (end-state check, e.g. DB row exists).
- Tool selection and argument accuracy.
- Steps, tokens, latency, cost per task.
- Recovery from injected tool failures.
- Safety: refusal of disallowed actions, injection resistance.
- pass@k (any of k succeed) vs pass^k (all k succeed) for reliability.

topics.title: Guardrails, Monitoring & Feedback Loops
topics.summary: Input/output validation layers and production monitoring that turns real usage into improvements.
topics.key_intuition: Defence in depth: validate inputs (length, language, injection heuristics), constrain outputs (schema, allow-lists, moderation), and monitor in production (error rate, refusal rate, cost, latency, thumbs-down) with alerts.
topics.pitfalls: Relying on an LLM guardrail as the only control; guardrails that block legitimate users with no appeal path; no sampling of production conversations for review.
topics.notes:
### Guardrails, Monitoring & Feedback Loops
- Category: 7. Evals & Observability
- Difficulty: Medium

### Layers
- Pre-model: size limits, PII detection, topic filters, rate limits.
- Model: system policy, structured output.
- Post-model: schema validation, content moderation, citation check, regex for secrets.
- Action: policy engine for tool calls (allow-list, spend limits, approval).
- Feedback: thumbs, corrections, escalations -> labelled dataset -> eval set.

topics.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
topics.summary: Know the standard threat list for LLM systems and the main mitigation for each.
topics.key_intuition: LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning, LLM05 Improper Output Handling, LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, LLM09 Misinformation, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption (2025 list).
topics.pitfalls: Treating model output as trusted (XSS, SQL injection, command injection through generated content); giving agents broad permissions; unlimited token usage enabling denial-of-wallet.
topics.notes:
### OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
- Category: 8. Safety & Security
- Difficulty: Medium

### Mitigation cheat sheet
- Injection: separate instructions from data, least privilege, human approval for risky actions.
- Output handling: encode/sanitise output, parameterise SQL, never eval or exec model text.
- Excessive agency: minimal tool set, scoped credentials, confirm destructive actions.
- Vector weaknesses: ACLs on retrieval, validate ingested documents.
- Unbounded consumption: max_tokens, per-user quotas, timeouts, loop limits.
- Supply chain: pin/verify models, MCP servers and packages.

topics.title: Prompt Injection & the Lethal Trifecta
topics.summary: How direct and indirect prompt injection works against agents, and architectural defences that actually hold.
topics.key_intuition: Models cannot reliably distinguish instructions from data. An agent is at serious risk when it combines (1) access to private data, (2) exposure to untrusted content, and (3) the ability to communicate externally. Remove at least one leg of that trifecta.
topics.pitfalls: "Ignore malicious instructions" prompts as the only defence; letting a browsing/email-reading agent also send email or make HTTP requests with private data; rendering markdown images from model output (data exfiltration via URLs).
topics.notes:
### Prompt Injection & the Lethal Trifecta
- Category: 8. Safety & Security
- Difficulty: Hard

### Defences
- Least privilege and per-task scoped credentials.
- Separate agents: one reads untrusted content with no powerful tools, another acts on a sanitised, structured summary.
- Human approval for actions with side effects or external communication.
- Egress allow-lists; strip/deny auto-loaded remote images and links from output.
- Treat all retrieved text, tool results and MCP descriptions as untrusted.
- Red-team with known injection corpora in your evals.

topics.title: Tool Permissions, Sandboxing & Human-in-the-Loop
topics.summary: Containing what an agent can do: scopes, sandboxes, approval gates, audit logs.
topics.key_intuition: Assume the agent will eventually be tricked or wrong. Limit blast radius: run code in isolated containers with no secrets and restricted network, grant tools the user's permissions only, and require approval for irreversible actions.
topics.pitfalls: Shared long-lived API keys inside the agent environment; auto-approving all tool calls; no audit trail; approvals that show the model's description instead of the real action and arguments.
topics.notes:
### Tool Permissions, Sandboxing & Human-in-the-Loop
- Category: 8. Safety & Security
- Difficulty: Hard

### Controls
- Risk tiers: read-only (auto), reversible write (log), irreversible/financial/external (approve).
- Approval UI shows exact arguments and a diff.
- Sandboxes: containers/microVMs (e.g. Docker, gVisor, Firecracker), ephemeral FS, network egress policy.
- Short-lived scoped tokens (OAuth on-behalf-of).
- Immutable audit log: who/what/when/inputs/outputs.
- Kill switch and per-run budgets.

topics.title: Privacy, PII Handling & Compliance for AI Features
topics.summary: Handling personal and confidential data when sending content to model providers and storing conversations.
topics.key_intuition: Know where data goes: provider retention and training policies, region, sub-processors. Minimise what you send, redact where possible, and apply the same access controls to embeddings and chat logs as to the source data.
topics.pitfalls: Logging full prompts forever; using consumer-tier APIs for business data; forgetting deletion requests must also remove vectors, caches and traces.
topics.notes:
### Privacy, PII Handling & Compliance for AI Features
- Category: 8. Safety & Security
- Difficulty: Medium

### Practices
- Use enterprise endpoints with zero-retention / no-training terms (Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex, vendor enterprise plans).
- PII redaction before logging (and optionally before the call).
- Data classification decides which model/region is allowed.
- Retention periods and deletion pipeline covering DB, vector index, caches, traces.
- Be aware of regulation: GDPR/DPDP, SOC 2, HIPAA, EU AI Act risk categories.
- Disclose AI use to users and provide feedback/appeal channels.

topics.title: Reliability: Retries, Fallbacks, Model Routing & LLM Gateways
topics.summary: Keeping AI features available when providers rate-limit, time out or degrade.
topics.key_intuition: Provider outages and 429s are normal. Use timeouts, exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, and a fallback model/provider. A gateway centralises keys, routing, budgets, caching and logging.
topics.pitfalls: Retrying non-idempotent tool executions; fallback model with different behaviour that breaks parsers; retry storms without jitter; no per-provider rate-limit awareness.
topics.notes:
### Reliability: Retries, Fallbacks, Model Routing & LLM Gateways
- Category: 9. LLMOps & Production
- Difficulty: Medium

### Gateway features
- Unified API across providers; key management.
- Routing by cost/latency/health; automatic fallback.
- Budgets and rate limits per team/user.
- Caching, logging, redaction.
- Options: LiteLLM, Portkey, Azure API Management AI gateway, Cloudflare AI Gateway, OpenRouter.
- In .NET add Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience (Polly v8) to the HttpClient used by the LLM client.

topics.title: Prompting vs RAG vs Fine-Tuning (LoRA, Distillation)
topics.summary: Deciding which lever to pull to improve an AI feature.
topics.key_intuition: Try in order: better prompt and examples, then retrieval/tools for missing knowledge, then fine-tuning for style, format, latency or cost. Fine-tuning teaches behaviour, not fresh facts. LoRA trains small adapter matrices instead of all weights.
topics.pitfalls: Fine-tuning to inject changing knowledge; tiny low-quality datasets; no baseline to compare against; forgetting to re-evaluate after base model upgrades.
topics.notes:
### Prompting vs RAG vs Fine-Tuning (LoRA, Distillation)
- Category: 9. LLMOps & Production
- Difficulty: Hard

### Decision guide
- Missing/changing facts -> RAG or tools.
- Wrong tone/format/consistency -> few-shot, then fine-tune.
- Too slow/expensive -> distil a large model's outputs into a small fine-tuned model.
- Domain-specific classification at scale -> fine-tune small model.
- Need hundreds to thousands of high-quality examples; hold out an eval set.
- Preference tuning (DPO) for style/safety alignment.

topics.title: Local & Open-Weight Models: Ollama, vLLM & Quantization
topics.summary: Running models yourself for privacy, cost control, offline use and experimentation.
topics.key_intuition: Ollama and llama.cpp make local dev trivial; vLLM serves open models at scale with continuous batching and PagedAttention. Quantization (8-bit, 4-bit) shrinks memory with small quality loss.
topics.pitfalls: Assuming local equals free (GPU cost, ops); comparing a quantized small model to a frontier model on hard tasks; exposing an unauthenticated inference port.
topics.notes:
### Local & Open-Weight Models: Ollama, vLLM & Quantization
- Category: 9. LLMOps & Production
- Difficulty: Medium

### Quick start
- ollama run llama3.1 ; the OpenAI-compatible endpoint is http://localhost:11434/v1.
- Use the same IChatClient / AI SDK interface so dev uses local and prod uses hosted.
- Memory rule of thumb: parameters x bytes-per-weight (4-bit ~ 0.5 bytes) plus KV cache.
- Good for: embeddings, classification, privacy-sensitive prototypes, CI tests.

topics.title: Latency Optimisation & Deploying AI Services
topics.summary: Reducing time-to-first-token and total latency, and deploying AI backends safely.
topics.key_intuition: Stream everything, shrink prompts, parallelise independent calls, cache prefixes, use smaller models for non-critical steps, and move slow work off the request path. Deploy like any service: containers, health checks, config-driven models, canary releases.
topics.pitfalls: Sequential tool calls that could be parallel; serverless cold starts plus long streams hitting platform timeouts; hard-coded model names; no cost alerts.
topics.notes:
### Latency Optimisation & Deploying AI Services
- Category: 9. LLMOps & Production
- Difficulty: Medium

### Checklist
- Measure TTFT, tokens/sec, p95 total latency per route.
- Parallel tool calls and Task.WhenAll / Promise.all for independent retrievals.
- Speculative/early UI: show retrieved sources before the answer completes.
- Deploy: Docker multi-stage, env-based secrets (Key Vault), readiness probes, autoscale on concurrency not CPU.
- Feature flags for model/prompt rollout; instant rollback.
- Budget alerts on provider spend.

topics.title: Agentic Coding Workflows: Copilot Agent, Claude Code & Cursor
topics.summary: Using coding agents effectively: planning, context files, tool permissions, verification.
topics.key_intuition: Treat the agent like a fast junior engineer with no memory: give it clear goals, the files that matter, repo conventions (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / copilot-instructions.md), and a way to verify its work (tests, type-check, lint).
topics.pitfalls: Accepting large diffs unread; letting the agent run destructive commands unapproved; vague prompts; no tests so nothing proves the change works.
topics.notes:
### Agentic Coding Workflows: Copilot Agent, Claude Code & Cursor
- Category: 10. AI-Assisted Engineering
- Difficulty: Easy

### Workflow
1. Explore & plan first (ask for a plan, review it).
2. Small, scoped tasks; commit often so you can revert.
3. Keep an AGENTS.md with build/test commands, architecture, conventions, gotchas.
4. Let it run tests/typecheck and iterate on failures.
5. Review diffs like a PR; check security-sensitive code by hand.
6. Use sub-agents / parallel sessions for independent tasks; use MCP servers for docs, DB schema, issue tracker.

topics.title: Spec-Driven Development & Reviewing AI-Generated Code
topics.summary: Writing specs and acceptance tests that guide agents, and a review checklist for AI-written code.
topics.key_intuition: The clearer the spec and tests, the better the agent. Write requirements, edge cases and acceptance criteria first; ask the agent to implement against them. Review for correctness, security, and maintainability, not just whether it compiles.
topics.pitfalls: Hallucinated APIs and packages (verify they exist); subtle logic bugs that pass shallow tests; copy-pasted insecure patterns; unnecessary abstractions and dead code.
topics.notes:
### Spec-Driven Development & Reviewing AI-Generated Code
- Category: 10. AI-Assisted Engineering
- Difficulty: Medium

### Review checklist
- Does it do what the spec says, including failure paths?
- Are inputs validated, queries parameterised, authz enforced?
- Are dependencies real, maintained and licensed?
- Tests meaningful (not asserting the implementation)?
- Concurrency, resource disposal, error handling, logging.
- Performance traps (N+1, unbounded loops, allocations).
- Keep PRs small; require human sign-off.

topics.title: Testing AI Features & Using AI to Write Tests
topics.summary: How to unit/integration test non-deterministic LLM code and leverage agents for test generation.
topics.key_intuition: Test the deterministic shell with ordinary tests (fake IChatClient returning canned responses), and the model behaviour with evals. Record/replay LLM responses for stable CI.
topics.pitfalls: Live LLM calls in unit tests (flaky, slow, costly); snapshot-testing free-text; tests that only check that "something" was returned.
topics.notes:
### Testing AI Features & Using AI to Write Tests
- Category: 10. AI-Assisted Engineering
- Difficulty: Medium

### Layers
- Unit: tool functions, prompt builders, parsers, routers with a fake model client.
- Integration: WebApplicationFactory with fake provider; contract tests for tool schemas.
- Evals: nightly job on real models with thresholds.
- Property/fuzz: injection strings, huge inputs, unicode.
- AI-generated tests: ask for edge cases and mutation-style checks, then verify they fail when the code is broken.

topics.title: Design an Enterprise RAG Chatbot
topics.summary: System design walk-through for a secure, multi-tenant, citation-backed knowledge assistant.
topics.key_intuition: Clarify scope (sources, users, freshness, ACLs, languages, SLAs), then design: ingestion pipeline, permission-aware index, retrieval + rerank, generation with citations, feedback and evals, observability, cost controls.
topics.pitfalls: Forgetting document-level permissions; no freshness/incremental indexing story; no evaluation plan; skipping failure modes (no answer found, provider outage).
topics.notes:
### Design an Enterprise RAG Chatbot
- Category: 11. AI System Design
- Difficulty: Hard

### Components
- Connectors (SharePoint, Confluence, Drive, DB) -> queue -> parser/chunker -> embedder -> vector + keyword index with ACL metadata.
- Query service: auth -> query rewrite -> hybrid retrieve with ACL filter -> rerank -> LLM -> citations.
- Caches: embeddings, retrieval, prompt prefix.
- Async: re-index on change events, content-hash dedupe.
- Quality: offline evals, online thumbs, sampled review.
- Scale numbers: docs count, chunks (docs x chunks/doc), QPS, tokens/query, cost/day.
- Failure: fallback model, "I don't know" path, degraded keyword-only search.

topics.title: Design a Coding Agent
topics.summary: Architecture for an agent that reads a repo, edits files, runs tests and opens PRs safely.
topics.key_intuition: Core loop with tools (read/search/edit/run), a sandboxed workspace per task, repo indexing for retrieval, test-driven verification, and strict permission/approval layers.
topics.pitfalls: Running in the user's real environment with secrets; unbounded loops; giant file reads blowing the context; no way to resume or audit.
topics.notes:
### Design a Coding Agent
- Category: 11. AI System Design
- Difficulty: Hard

### Design
- Task API + queue; worker spins up an ephemeral container with the repo checked out.
- Tools: search (ripgrep + embeddings), view file ranges, apply patch, run command (allow-list), run tests.
- Context management: repo map, compaction, notes file.
- Verification loop: tests/lint/typecheck; stop when green or budget hit.
- Output: branch + PR with explanation; human review required.
- Observability: full trajectory trace; cost per task; success rate by task type.
- Security: no network except package mirror, scoped Git token, secret scanning.

topics.title: Design an AI Customer Support Agent with Human Handoff
topics.summary: Agent that resolves tickets using knowledge base and account tools, escalating when unsure.
topics.key_intuition: Route intent first, ground answers in KB via RAG, use authenticated read tools for account info, require confirmation for actions (refund, cancel), and hand off to a human with full context when confidence is low or policy requires.
topics.pitfalls: Letting the agent promise refunds it cannot grant; no escalation triggers; losing conversation context at handoff; measuring only deflection rate instead of resolution quality and CSAT.
topics.notes:
### Design an AI Customer Support Agent with Human Handoff
- Category: 11. AI System Design
- Difficulty: Hard

### Flow
Intent router -> (FAQ: RAG) | (Account: tools) | (Action: policy engine + approval) | (Escalate: summary + transcript to human queue).

### Metrics
Resolution rate, escalation rate, CSAT, time-to-resolution, hallucination/policy-violation rate, cost per ticket.

### Safeguards
Policy as code (refund limits), audit log, PII redaction, injection-resistant ticket ingestion, tone guidelines.

topics.title: Design an LLM Gateway / AI Platform
topics.summary: Shared internal service giving teams governed access to many models.
topics.key_intuition: A single choke point for auth, routing, quotas, caching, safety filters and observability across providers, exposing a stable OpenAI-compatible API to internal teams.
topics.pitfalls: Gateway becoming a latency/availability bottleneck; per-team cost attribution missing; logging sensitive prompts in clear text.
topics.notes:
### Design an LLM Gateway / AI Platform
- Category: 11. AI System Design
- Difficulty: Hard

### Features
- Auth (service identity / JWT) and team budgets.
- Model catalog, routing and fallback policies, A/B.
- Token-aware rate limiting and quotas.
- Request/response cache, prompt-cache hints.
- Guardrails/PII redaction plugins.
- Usage metering, chargeback dashboards, audit.
- Streaming passthrough, high availability (stateless, horizontal scale), config hot-reload.

topics.title: Capstone 1: RAG Q&A over Your Own Docs (Next.js + pgvector)
topics.summary: Build and deploy a full-stack RAG app with ingestion, hybrid retrieval, streaming chat, citations and an eval suite.
topics.key_intuition: Goal: prove end-to-end skill. Deliver ingestion CLI, Postgres + pgvector schema, hybrid search with reranking, streaming chat UI with citations, auth + per-user limits, and a 50-question eval run in CI.
topics.pitfalls: Skipping the eval set; hard-coding keys; no README showing architecture and trade-offs (recruiters read this).
topics.notes:
### Capstone 1: RAG Q&A over Your Own Docs (Next.js + pgvector)
- Category: 12. Capstone Projects
- Difficulty: Hard

### Definition of done
- [ ] Ingest PDFs/Markdown with metadata and content-hash dedupe
- [ ] Hybrid retrieval + rerank, ACL filter
- [ ] Streaming Next.js chat with source citations
- [ ] Tracing (Langfuse/OpenTelemetry) and cost per request
- [ ] Eval script: recall@k, faithfulness; results in README
- [ ] Dockerfile + deployment
- [ ] Write-up: architecture diagram, decisions, failure cases

topics.title: Capstone 2: Tool-Using Agent with a Custom MCP Server (.NET or TypeScript)
topics.summary: Expose a real backend (orders, tickets, or this app's topics) as an MCP server and drive it with an agent that has approvals and audit logs.
topics.key_intuition: Shows protocol knowledge, secure tool design and agent engineering together: scoped tools, schema validation, human approval for writes, trace of every call.
topics.pitfalls: Exposing raw SQL as a tool; no auth on the HTTP transport; giving write tools without confirmation.
topics.notes:
### Capstone 2: Tool-Using Agent with a Custom MCP Server (.NET or TypeScript)
- Category: 12. Capstone Projects
- Difficulty: Hard

### Definition of done
- [ ] MCP server with 4+ tools and 1+ resource (stdio and Streamable HTTP)
- [ ] Authz per user; input validation; idempotent writes
- [ ] Agent client with max-steps/budget and approval step for mutations
- [ ] Audit log + OpenTelemetry traces
- [ ] Unit tests with fake model; 20-case agent eval
- [ ] Demo video/GIF and README

topics.title: Capstone 3: Multi-Agent Research Assistant with Evals & Tracing
topics.summary: Orchestrator that plans, fans out researcher agents, synthesises a cited report, and is measured by an eval harness.
topics.key_intuition: Demonstrates orchestration, context engineering (sub-agents return condensed findings), long-running job design, and measurable quality/cost tradeoffs versus a single-agent baseline.
topics.pitfalls: No single-agent baseline to compare; uncited claims; unbounded fan-out cost.
topics.notes:
### Capstone 3: Multi-Agent Research Assistant with Evals & Tracing
- Category: 12. Capstone Projects
- Difficulty: Hard

### Definition of done
- [ ] Planner + parallel researcher workers + synthesiser/critic
- [ ] Job API with progress streaming and cancellation
- [ ] Budgets (steps, tokens, time) enforced
- [ ] Report with citations; citation-check step
- [ ] Eval harness comparing single vs multi-agent on quality, cost, latency
- [ ] Trace screenshots and lessons-learned section in README
